extractions.value: Clinical features (stiffness and rigidity began in axial muscles, slowly involving proximal limb muscles; painful spasms triggered by sudden noise, movement or emotional upset; normal neurological and intellective functions; normal neuroradiological investigations); positive anti-GAD antibodies in serum; EMG showing spontaneous firing of motor unit action potentials involving antagonistic muscles culminating in spasm.
extractions.quote: Our observation fulfils both the clinical as well as the electrophysiological criteria of SMS. In fact, the stiffness and rigidity began in axial muscles, slowly involving the proximal limb muscles; the painful spasms were triggered by sudden noise, movement or emotional upset; the neurological and intellective functions were normal; no abnormalities were disclosed by neuroradiological investigations [11]. EMG examination showed the constantly found electrophysiological counterpart of this syndrome, i.e. the spontaneous firing of motor unit action potentials involving antagonistic muscles, culminating in spasm induced by the above causes.

extractions.value: Needle EMG of antagonistic muscle pairs; motor and sensory nerve conduction studies of four nerves (right median and peroneal, left ulnar and tibial); silent period determined in tibialis anterior during voluntary contraction stimulating the peroneal nerve at the head of the fibula by an electrical shock of 0.1 ms duration; H reflex from soleus; H-M recruitment curve; H-H recovery curve by paired shock (conditioning stimulus 0.8 of motor threshold, test stimulus = Hmax/2); H/M ratio; polysynaptic flexion reflexes RII and RIII of short head of biceps femoris and extension (RPPS) of soleus; presynaptic inhibition index (vibration index); Ib soleus H reflex inhibition; Ia H reflex antagonistic inhibition; polysomnography.
extractions.quote: The silent period was determined in the tibialis anterior muscle during a voluntary contraction stimulating the peroneal nerve at the head of the fibula by an electrical shock of 0.1 ms duration. An H reflex with a normal latency was obtained from the soleus muscle. The H-M recruitment curve showed a normal shape, as did the H-H recovery curve by paired shock [conditioning stimulus 0.8 of the motor threshold (MT) test stimulus = Hmax/2]. The H/M ratio was normal, i.e. 0.45. The polysynaptic flexion reflexes RII and RIII of the short head of the biceps femoris muscle [8] and extension (RPPS) of the soleus [15] were obtained by specific stimuli at the appropriate sites of stimulation... The presynaptic inhibition index [4] showed a reduced vibration index of 86.6. The Ib soleus H reflex inhibition [19] was replaced by a facilitation of the H reflex in the interstimulus delay of 1-6 ms... and Ia H reflex antagonistic inhibition [21] showed a normal inhibition with a reduction of H reflex in the interstimulus delay of 1-5 ms.

The polysynaptic flexion reflexes RII and RIII of the short head of the biceps femoris muscle [8] and extension (RPPS) of the soleus [15] were obtained by specific stimuli at the appropriate sites of stimulation, without any enlargement of the receptive field, but a reflex activity was also simultaneously recorded in the antagonistic muscles (Fig. 1). The same activities showed a lack of the habituation phenomenon, i.e. they persisted when the rate of stimulation was of the amount inducing disappearance of the reflex activity in the normal subject (Fig. 1).
Brain CT and MRI were normal.

extractions.value: Polysomnography showed disrupted sleep with excessive awakenings and protracted periods of nocturnal myoclonus. Presynaptic inhibition index showed a reduced vibration index of 86.6. Ib soleus H reflex inhibition was replaced by facilitation in the interstimulus delay of 1-6 ms. Ia H reflex antagonistic inhibition was normal. H/M ratio was normal (0.45).
extractions.quote: In addition to excessive awakenings, protracted periods of nocturnal myoclonus were recorded. The presynaptic inhibition index [4] showed a reduced vibration index of 86.6. The Ib soleus H reflex inhibition [19] was replaced by a facilitation of the H reflex in the interstimulus delay of 1-6 ms (Fig. 2), and Ia H reflex antagonistic inhibition [21] showed a normal inhibition with a reduction of H reflex in the interstimulus delay of 1-5 ms.
